detail: Seeded auth/01 planned. `werk ticket move auth/01 blocked --reason ...` exits 2: 'unknown flag --reason', usage 'ticket restore <number> [--actor you]'. Only the restore subverb exists in src/verbs/ticket.ts; move, archive and list are not built (not my naming error: grep and help confirm). This is the CLI subverb that step 27 names, so it is werk/27's own job.

`werk ticket move auth/01 blocked` exits 2 with 'ticket needs the subverb restore and one number', not a message that asks for a reason; `ticket list` does not exist either. The move subverb is missing.
Seeded auth/02 planned (ready, never archived). `werk ticket restore 02` exits 1 and board.jsonl is byte-identical; `werk ticket restore 99` exits 1 and the log is byte-identical.

`werk ticket archive auth/03` (done ticket) exits 2 with 'ticket needs the subverb restore and one number', not a 'done ticket cannot be archived' message; archive and list subverbs do not exist. (The board fold has an ARCHIVABLE rule, but no CLI reaches it.)
`werk ticket move auth/02 blocked --reason ...` exits 2 ('unknown flag --reason'); archive and list also missing, so the listing and the actor check cannot be reached.

Planned app with fake agent (3 tickets), moved 01 to building and 02 to done, added a decided card 'two' under app and re-ran `werk plan app`. One plan 'app', spec text covers new card, ticket 03 kept its number with rewritten title, new ticket 04 added, no repeated number, 01 still building and 02 still done with their ticket files byte-identical.

Planned two tickets, removed card 'two' (`remove two --actor you`), re-planned with a drop of ticket 2. Ticket app/02 is archived with reason 'the current spec no longer needs it' (archive by plan); `werk ticket restore 02 --actor you` brings it back to ready under its number.

With `werk serve` running (the cited-card watcher lives in the server), `propose one --title` + `accept one --actor you` moved ready ticket app/01 to blocked; reason names #one and 'title changed'. A new `werk plan app` returned it to ready with an empty reason and its file cites the card. I polled up to 8 s for the server's watcher to write the mark.

With the server running: `say one` (note) left ready app/01 and building app/02 unblocked with no reason. After a body change (`propose --ops` + accept) app/01 moved to blocked with a reason naming #one and 'body changed'; the building ticket stayed building with no reason.

With the server running, adding a decided card 'extra' under app set plan app uncited to ['extra'] on the board; both tickets stay ready with no reason; `werk ticket-check <tickets dir> --root app --spec ...` prints the cards-cited failure naming 'extra'. Note: the plan itself is not re-run; reporting happens via the board record and ticket-check.

Real server, seeded board log. Columns in order Blocked, Ready, Building, Merging, Done, each card in its column; blockers show ⊘2, retries show ↻3. `werk ticket move` does not exist (see 27.1), so the test tries it and falls back to appending the ticket.moved event (ready to building, actor you) to the board log; the page redrew without reload (window flag kept) and the card moved. The CLI part of this step cannot run via a real command.

At 1000px the full title needs at least 4 lines; the card shows 2 lines with line-clamp 2 and cut text; hover shows the title attribute with the full title; click opens a drawer below the board, header has code r/02 above the full-title heading.

With a live builder pid the card has a corner live dot; first line of title starts about 8px right of the dot (0 < gap <= 12). After killing the process (no session end written) the dot disappears within 15 s and the first line moves back to the left edge (equals other cards' text left). A building ticket whose pid is dead or absent never shows a dot (second test '44.3 (no process)').

Drawer of building ticket with 81 log lines: scroller clientHeight < scrollHeight (fixed height), log box above ticket text, time format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', sidebar regions Cites, Blockers, Retries, Checks, Stories, Touches; Decisions lists #role-format as proposal; click #root opens /map/root; after returning and folding the sidebar, a reload keeps data-mode=rail; when the ticket moves to ready the Live log is gone but ticket text and sidebar remain. After goBack the drawer was already open, so I opened it only when closed.

At 600px the board scrolls sideways (scrollWidth > clientWidth), all 5 columns >= 200px, done column starts off screen and a sideways scroll brings it into view; at 1600px the scrollbar is gone, columns have equal width and fill the board width.
